title: Incomplete paged-feed preview is stored as a normal job; a move then finalizes with a partial catalog
reproduction:
Site /tmp/epm-a-import-a (WP 7.1.2, Elementor 4.3.3, PHP 8.4.26, SQLite).
Command: S=/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-elementor-podcast-manager/981ff890-e6a5-5b32-be23-efa8394adebf/scratchpad/audit/import-a; $S/wpq eval-file $S/imp01-pagination.php (output in $S/imp01-output.txt).
Each case is a 3-page feed of 3 items (newest first), served through EPM_Test_HTTP::$routes with offline=true. The move is started with purpose=move and confirm_owner, in external mode.
- page 2 = HTTP 500 (with copy media): requests p1,p2. Preview episodes '3 (real catalog 9)', completeness keys [], job 'ready / 3'. Final 'done done=3/3', finish_move ran (moved_in/locked [true,true]), hosting mode 'self', 3 of 9 episodes on the site, 3 items in own feed.
- timeout (WP_Error 'cURL error 28'): identical result, 3 of 9.
- page 2 invalid XML (truncated at 400 bytes): identical result, 3 of 9.
- page 2 empty but rel=next to p3: requests p1,p2 only; 3 of 6, moved.
- relative next 'p2.xml': requests ["…/relative/p1.xml","https://p2.xml"]; 3 of 9, moved.
- root-relative '/audit/rootrel/p2.xml': request "https://audit/rootrel/p2.xml"; preview 3 of 9.
- epm_import_max_pages=3 on 5 pages: preview 6 of 10, moved with 6 of 10.
- default cap on 55 pages: p1..p50 fetched, preview 50 of 55, job 'ready / 50'.
CLI: with scratch/scenario-imp01-cli.php active, `wpq podcast import https://feeds.example.test/audit-cli/p1.xml --move --owner` printed "CLI move show — 3 episodes (0 already here)" and "Success: 3 new, 0 updated, 0 unchanged, 0 skipped, 0 failed." Afterwards moved_in=true locked=true (output in $S/imp01-cli-output.txt).
user_impact: A transient error on page N of a paged feed (SoundCloud serves 500 items per page), a relative next link, an empty page or the 50-page cap produces a preview that looks complete ("3 episodes"). A move then finishes normally: the site switches to self-hosting, locks the feed and publishes only part of the back catalog. The docs tell users to redirect the old feed and close the old account after a move. Doing that would make directories treat the missing episodes as removed, and the back catalog would be lost for good. No UI, CLI or job field tells the user anything is missing.
proposed_fix:
1. Track pages explicitly in the job: pages_loaded, next_url, stop_reason (complete | http_error | transport_error | parse_error | empty_page_with_next | cycle | page_limit | budget) and the concrete error. Return complete=false plus the reason from preview(), and show it in the Hosting screen, the setup assistant and the CLI (non-zero exit or a warning).
2. Resolve next hrefs against the page URL with WP_Http::make_absolute_url( $next, $page_url ) (honour xml:base).
3. Treat an empty page that has rel=next as an error or continue with a bound, instead of a silent stop.
4. Fetch pages incrementally across requests (see IMP-N1) so a failed page can be retried and resumed from next_url.
5. In step(), never call finish_move() for an incomplete catalog: end in a distinct status (e.g. done_partial) that lists what is missing, and require an explicit, informed override to finalize.
notes:
Cleared inside IMP-01:
- URL cycle (p3 back to p2): every page fetched once, 9 of 9 episodes.
- Duplicate GUIDs across pages: preview.duplicates lists 1 duplicate, the page-1 (newer) copy is kept (date 2026-01-12, original notes), and the import creates 9 of 9 with 1 copy each.
- Resume after the page-2 error (fixed page, second preview + mirror import): preview 9 / existing 3, created 6, unchanged 3, 9 distinct GUIDs, max 1 copy.

Relative atom:link hrefs are legal IRI references in Atom (RFC 4287, xml:base); this is background knowledge, not fetched during the audit.

docs/HOSTING.md §5 says paged feeds "are followed up to 50 pages" and never mentions that a stop is silent.

title: One AJAX preview loads every page into memory; the default 50-page cap exceeds stock PHP-FPM memory and proxy timeouts, and every step re-reads the full catalog
evidence:
includes/ImportJob.php:279: $parsed['items'] = array_merge( $parsed['items'], $more['items'] ); inside the page loop (269-282), all pages in one request.
ImportJob.php:300: file_put_contents( $file, (string) wp_json_encode( $items ) ), the whole catalog encoded at once. The fatal happened at wp-includes/functions.php:4444 (wp_json_encode).
ImportJob.php:223-232 items(): json_decode( file_get_contents( $file ), true ) is called on every step() (ImportJob.php:478).
No set_time_limit and no byte, time or page budget besides the 50-page filter.
reproduction:
1. CLI (wp-cli, baseline 68 MB), items with 1.5 KB notes: `EPA_MEM=<limit> $S/wpm 512M eval-file $S/imp01-perf.php <pages> 500 1500`.
   - 20×500 (10,000 items, 17.3 MB XML): 1.17 s, peak 124.7 MB, job file 20.9 MB. At memory_limit 128M: "Fatal error: Allowed memory size of 134217728 bytes exhausted (tried to allocate 21696512 bytes) in wp-includes/functions.php on line 4444".
   - 50×500 (25,000 items, 43.3 MB): 3.7 s, peak 206.1 MB.
2. Real AJAX through nginx 1.24 + php-fpm 8.4 with stock php.ini (memory_limit 128M, max_execution_time 30) on port 8968, using scratch/scenario-perf.php and perf.json. Results in $S/perf-ajax.log:
   - 5 pages: 0.43 s, 21.6 MB
   - 10 pages: 0.70 s, 35.2 MB
   - 20 pages: 1.25 s, 62.4 MB
   - 35 pages: 2.08 s, 103.5 MB
   - 50 pages: HTTP 500 "There has been a critical error on this website." after 2.35 s; PHP log: Allowed memory size of 134217728 bytes exhausted.
3. 50 pages × 50 items with 1.3 s latency per page: `curl … action=epm_import_preview` returned "HTTP 504 60.023331s" (nginx default fastcgi_read_timeout). PHP kept running (time=65.35s) and saved the job: "ready total=2500".
4. Steps on the 10,000-item job via AJAX: 3 steps of 0.57-0.59 s each, each at peak 67.8 MB, for 10 items.
user_impact: Large paged catalogs, which are exactly the shows that use paging, cannot be previewed on common hosting. At 128M the admin gets a fatal error, which the UI shows as "Something went wrong. Check your connection and try again." (epm-hosting.js:59-60). Behind a 60 s proxy the browser gets a 504 while PHP silently saves a job. Retrying repeats the full cost. Large catalogs also pay about 0.3 s and 60+ MB per step just to re-read the file.
proposed_fix: Fetch one page (or a byte/time budget) per request and keep a cursor (next_url, pages_loaded) in the job. Append items to the job file per page (JSON Lines) instead of encoding everything at once. Keep a total budget for pages, bytes, time and memory that stops with an explicit 'limited' state (see IMP-01). Let step() read only the needed slice (a line offset index) instead of the whole file. Coordinate with IMP-04, which covers the download limits.
test_plan: A measurement script (like scratch/imp01-perf.php plus an AJAX run under php-fpm 128M) in CI or a documented perf job: 50×500 items must preview without exceeding a set memory budget (e.g. under 64 MB above baseline) and without any single request longer than N s. Assert that step() memory does not grow with catalog size (1,000 vs 10,000 items). Assert the 504/latency case resumes from the cursor instead of restarting.

title: Import/sync lock is not mutually exclusive and job state is not bound to the lock: duplicate episodes, lost/backwards progress, finished jobs marked failed, running imports replaced
evidence:
Lock, includes/ImportJob.php:74-94 at b1076c8:
  // add_option() fails when the row exists: an atomic test-and-set.
  if ( add_option( self::LOCK, time() . ':' . $owner, '', false ) ) {...}
  ... if ( $since > 0 && time() - $since > self::lock_ttl() ) { delete_option( self::LOCK ); if ( add_option( ... ) ) ...
In WP 7.1.2 core (site/wp-includes/option.php):
- 1119-1124: add_option skips the existence check when notoptions[$option] is set.
- 1140: do_action('add_option').
- 1142: "INSERT INTO ... ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE `option_value` = VALUES(`option_value`)" overwrites an existing row and returns true.
- 1243-1250: delete_option puts the option into notoptions.
refresh_lock (ImportJob.php:134-142) and release_lock (150-155) check first and then write or delete without a condition.

Job, step() (ImportJob.php:464-558):
- 465: $job = self::get() is read BEFORE 471 acquire_lock().
- 484-488: 'failed' is saved from that snapshot without a fresh read.
- 501: self::refresh_lock(); the return value is ignored.
- 533-552: re-reads status/token only, then 552 self::save( $job ), which writes the snapshot's position, counts and log.

preview() (241, 262, 355) and start() (416, 451) never take the lock. preview deletes the file of the job it read ($current) and overwrites the option.
Hosting.php:806 uses the same acquire_lock(); Hosting.php:921 ignores the refresh_lock() return.
Importer.php:66-90: guid_map() is built once per step. There is no fresh GUID check before create (Importer.php:168-169, 221).
admin/js/epm-hosting.js:561-563 auto-starts stepping when the Hosting screen opens on a running job; 458 polls again after 3000 ms when busy and 150 ms otherwise.
docs/HOSTING.md §4 claims "An import and a sync never run at the same time."
reproduction:
All runs use two (or three) separate OS processes synchronized by barrier files (scratch/barrier.php); no plugin code was changed.

1. Lock races: `$S/run-imp02-locks.sh <scenario> [$S/wpq2]`. Outputs: imp02-locks-sqlite.txt, imp02-locks-mariadb.txt, imp02-locks-mariadb-redis.txt.
   - fresh: both processes print "acquired":true (SQLite, MariaDB 10.11.14, MariaDB+Redis).
   - stale: both acquired. The event log shows "B deletes the lock row now; current value: …:E6DzuIWuIRyu", i.e. A's fresh lock.
   - refresh: A refresh_returned true and the lock row ends as A's value while B also holds acquired:true.
   - release: A's release deleted B's fresh lock; B "still owns after A released": false, lock row "".
   - loop: A (acquire, release, acquire) second acquire true, lock row changes from B's owner to A's; B refresh_lock false. No barrier inside plugin code is needed.
   - booted (`$S/run-booted-compare.sh`, imp02-booted.txt): a request booted while the lock was free, then A took the lock. SQLite and MariaDB without a cache: B acquired:false (correct). MariaDB + Redis persistent cache: "B notoptions says lock absent":true, B acquired:true, lock row changes from A's to B's, A "still owns": false.

2. Cron loop + AJAX step (`$S/run-imp02-steps.sh`, with nginx/php-fpm on 8968): A = ImportJob::run_in_background() in CLI, B = real admin-ajax epm_import_step. Result: "episodes: 40 posts for 30 GUIDs; GUIDs with duplicates: 10", while the job says "status=done … counts={created:30…}" (imp02-steps-sqlite.txt). The same run on MariaDB with a CLI step as B: 40 posts for 30 GUIDs (imp02-steps-mariadb.txt).

3. Job-state races (`$S/run-imp02-jobs.sh <scenario>`, imp02-jobs-sqlite*.txt):
   - failed-over-done: A finished (status done); B, which read the job before its lock, saved "status=failed … error=The stored feed data is missing".
   - failed-over-new: A cancelled and previewed another feed (token 4bKQ3V); B saved the old job as failed; start(new token) returned "WP_Error: This import expired"; the new job file was left orphaned.
   - backwards: A saved position 20 (created 20); B then saved "position=10/40 … counts={created:0, unchanged:10}".
   - preview-vs-start: A started and stepped (running, done=10); B's preview, which had read the 'ready' job, overwrote it. A's next step returned "ready done=0/1 title=Other show".
   - cancel-mid-batch: B cancelled after A created item 3; A still created 10 episodes; the job stayed cancelled (see IMP-N2).

4. No barriers at all:
   - `$S/run-imp02-natural.sh 600 2 0.15`: 609 posts for 600 GUIDs.
   - `$S/run-imp02-natural-js.sh 1500 1 0` (1 tab with the JS timing: 3 s after busy, 150 ms otherwise): 1509 posts for 1500 GUIDs.
   - Traced run (`run-imp02-natural-traced.sh 300 1 0`, natural-trace.log): 309 for 300. The trace shows AJAX writing lock …ItmLv9 at .9224 and the loop writing lock …ybCIfF over it at .9817. The loop's cached job had pos=0, so it saved position 10 with counts reset. Both then inserted race-012..race-020.
   - Site 2 (`$S/run-natural-site2.sh 1000`) with MariaDB+Redis: 1005 for 1000 (race-976..980). MariaDB without a cache: 0 duplicates, but counts 'unchanged 10' from the stale re-import.
   - Own feed after a run: 'guid race-012 in own feed: 2'.
user_impact:
When two steppers run the same job, the lock does not protect it. This happens with cron's run_in_background loop or `wp podcast import` while the admin opens Hosting & import (which auto-resumes stepping), with two tabs, or after a crashed request left a stale lock.
- Episodes are imported twice (same GUID twice in the site's own feed).
- The progress position can go backwards and the counters are overwritten.
- A finished import can show as 'failed'.
- A freshly checked feed can be replaced ("This import expired").
- A running import can be silently replaced by another preview.
The result screen and the CLI show normal counts, so duplicates go unnoticed. With a persistent object cache (Redis or Memcached, common on managed WordPress), even fresh requests overwrite a live lock.
notes: The Redis results use a minimal WP_Object_Cache drop-in written for this audit (scratch/object-cache-redis.php). Like common drop-ins, it keeps a per-request runtime copy in front of Redis; the booted result depends on that runtime copy of the shared notoptions array. On the SQLite site, WP-CLI processes and php-fpm workers shared one SQLite file; MariaDB results used CLI processes only (no web server on site 2). Cancel is never revived by a running step (the end-of-batch check works), and preview()/start() refuse a job whose status is already 'running' (code ImportJob.php:241-244, 418), except for the interleavings shown above.

title: Cancel does not stop the running batch: a mirror step keeps importing up to 10 items / 8 s after Cancel
evidence:
includes/ImportJob.php:500-526: the while loop over $items has no status, cancel or lock check per item. The only check is after the loop (530-537: wp_cache_delete( self::OPTION ... ); $fresh = self::get(); if ( 'running' !== $fresh['status'] ... ) return).
Batch size: $batch = $download ? 1 : 10 (482).
reproduction: `$S/run-imp02-jobs.sh cancel-mid-batch` (imp02-jobs-sqlite-2.txt). A runs step() on a 10-item mirror job; B calls ImportJob::cancel() after A created item 3. Output: [A] "A step returned":"cancelled done=0","episodes created by A":10 and "race episodes: 10 posts for 10 GUIDs". The job stays cancelled (no revival).
user_impact: After pressing Cancel, up to 7-9 more episodes appear, and the job then reports done=0. Minor, but it contradicts the expected cancel semantics: a running download may finish, then nothing more.
proposed_fix: Check a fresh job status and token, plus lock ownership, before each item (cheap direct DB read) and stop the loop immediately when cancelled. Keep the position consistent with what was actually imported.
test_plan: Two-process test: cancel after the 3rd wp_insert_post of a 10-item batch. Assert at most 1 further item is created and the job stays cancelled with position/counts matching the created episodes.

title: Per-item sync failures are invisible (status ok, success message) and not retried while the feed is unchanged
reproduction:
`$S/wpq eval-file $S/sync-audit.php itemfail`. Output: sync-audit-output.txt.
The insert of 'Episode sif-002' is vetoed via the wp_insert_post_empty_content filter (a DB error or a vetoing plugin).
1. Sync now: {"status":"ok","message":"2 new episodes."}; state "status=ok failures=0 … etag=set"; episodes {sif-001, sif-003}.
2. Filter removed, then two Hosting::run_scheduled_sync(): both requests 'conditional'; state msg "No new episodes."; episodes still {sif-001, sif-003}.
3. Only the next forced Sync now created sif-002.
user_impact: A mirrored episode that failed to import is silently missing. The dashboard and Readiness say the sync worked. The episode appears only when the host feed changes (the next new episode) or someone happens to press Sync now.
proposed_fix: Count failed and skipped outcomes. Report them in the message and state (e.g. status 'partial', with the titles and errors of the items), and surface them in Readiness and the admin notice. When any item failed, do not store ETag/Last-Modified (or keep a retry list of failed GUIDs), so the next scheduled run fetches the full feed and retries.
test_plan: Integration: veto one item, then assert the sync result/state reports 1 failed item with its title and status != ok. Remove the veto and run one scheduled sync: assert the item is created without a forced sync.
notes:
Per-item sync failure/partial retry coverage is pending.
Verification: tests/integration/audit-sync.php (failed item visible, validators withheld, retry on unchanged feed; 1.3.0 baseline fails).

title: Credentials/tokens in the host feed URL are published to anonymous visitors and copied onto every episode
user_impact: If a site mirrors a private or authenticated feed (members' or paid feeds, basic-auth staging feeds, tokenized private RSS), anonymous visitors can read the credentials from the page source or the feed redirect. The admin gets no warning. The secret also persists in postmeta of every episode, in exports and in backups. Precondition: an admin enters such a URL. The mirrored audio is public anyway, so the incremental leak is the credential (ongoing access, a possibly reused password).
proposed_fix: Detect userinfo and credential-like query parameters (auth, token, key, signature …) in the host feed URL, and warn at save time. Never output such a URL publicly: skip the discovery link, JSON-LD webFeed and subscribe link, and do not 301 to it (or require an explicit public feed URL). Store a normalized, credential-free identifier in source_feed meta (or a hash). Mask the URL in admin displays and messages.
notes: Private source hash/redirect tests exist; public HTML and REST redaction coverage is pending.
verification: 2026-10-01: tests/integration/hosting.php (legacy credentialed source hidden from anonymous REST, kept unchanged in storage and matched during removal checks). Regression reproduced before the repair and passed afterwards on the marked local test site.

title: <itunes:new-feed-url> is adopted without validating the new address; the site's 301 then points to a broken feed
user_impact: A typo or a premature new-feed-url at the host silently re-points the site's sync and the site's permanent redirect to a dead URL. Apps that follow the site's 301 update to the dead address. The sync that made the change reports plain success.
proposed_fix: Before adopting, fetch the announced URL: it must return 200, parse as RSS, and match the show (same podcast:guid, or overlapping item GUIDs). Adopt only after validation, and say so in the message. On failure, keep the old URL and report a warning. The same applies to 301/308 moves (already validated by the successful fetch).
notes: tests/integration/audit-sync.php (404, invalid RSS and an unrelated valid show keep both source and public redirect; original sync fails)

title: A stalled sync (WP-Cron not running) is reported as healthy
evidence:
includes/Readiness.php:347-358 at b1076c8:
  if ( 'error' === $state['status'] ) {...} elseif ( (int) $state['last_success'] > 0 ) { $add( 'ok', __( 'Last sync' ), sprintf( '%1$s ago — %2$s', human_time_diff( last_success ), message ) ); }
There is no comparison with the interval or wp_next_scheduled().
includes/AdminPages.php:295-296: the notice appears only when failures >= 3, and failures never increase if the sync never runs.
There is no DISABLE_WP_CRON or loopback check in includes/.
user_impact: On low-traffic sites, with DISABLE_WP_CRON, or with blocked loopback requests, new episodes from the host stop appearing, while the dashboard and Readiness show the sync as fine. Scheduled (future) imported episodes and the import's cron continuation also depend on WP-Cron.
proposed_fix: Warn (Readiness warning plus admin notice) when last_run or last_success is older than about 2× the interval, or the next epm_sync_feed event is overdue by more than the interval. Mention DISABLE_WP_CRON or loopback and link to the server-cron advice already in HOSTING.md. Show 'next sync' as overdue on the Hosting screen.
test_plan: Integration test: with the event overdue and last_success older than 2× the interval, Readiness reports a warning. With a fresh sync, OK. Also test DISABLE_WP_CRON defined in a subprocess.
notes: Verification: tests/integration/hosting.php (overdue warning and summary badge).

title: Date changes and removals of scheduled (future) episodes at the host are never applied: removed/rescheduled episodes still publish at the old time
evidence:
includes/Importer.php:286-294 (create only):
  $postarr['post_date_gmt'] = gmdate( 'Y-m-d H:i:s', $timestamp ); ... if ( 'publish' === $status && $timestamp > time() ) { $postarr['post_status'] = 'future'; }
Importer.php:318-337 values() has no date field, so write() never updates the post date.
Importer.php:524-528 draft_missing() only queries 'post_status' => 'publish', so imported 'future' posts are never considered.
reproduction:
`$S/wpq eval-file $S/sync-audit.php future` and `… dates` (sync-audit-output.txt):
- [keep] future item imported as 'future at 2026-10-02 21:24:45'. After the host removed it (2 syncs): 'future … publish_future_post cron=2026-10-02 21:24'.
- [draft] (missing=draft): same result, still future with a scheduled publish.
- Host moved the date +5 days: 'Up to date. post_date_gmt=2026-10-02 21:24:45 (host: 2026-10-07 21:24:45)'.
- Host corrected a past pubDate (sdt-01): 'Up to date. post_date_gmt=2026-03-29 00:30:00' (unchanged).
user_impact: If a host feed ever carries a future-dated item (a scheduled premiere, or a clock or time-zone mislabel), a later reschedule or withdrawal at the host is ignored. The site publishes the episode at the old time, possibly days early or after it was pulled. Corrected publish dates of existing episodes are also never mirrored, so ordering and dates stay wrong.
proposed_fix: Treat the publish date as an importer-managed field with the same local-edit hashing (update post_date/post_date_gmt only while unchanged locally). For imported posts in 'future' status that disappear from the feed, return them to draft on the next sync (regardless of the missing policy, or at least with missing=draft). Keep 'future' handling in the site's timezone as now.
notes:
Changed future dates and removal are not covered by a dedicated regression test yet.
Verification: tests/integration/audit-sync.php (managed date, publish event, removal of future episodes; 1.3.0 baseline fails).

title: Sync never follows rel="next": only the first page of a paged feed is synced
evidence:
includes/Hosting.php:818 $fetched = self::fetch( $url, $validators ); and 852 parse. The sync has no loop over $parsed['channel']['next'] (unlike ImportJob.php:264-282).
Hosting.php:977 stores 'items' => count( page 1 ).
user_impact: For paged feeds, edits at the host to older episodes (titles, notes, audio replacements) are never mirrored. New episodes (page 1) and the drafting safety are fine. If a host ever orders pages oldest-first, new episodes would never be seen; that is a hypothesis, not observed.
proposed_fix: Either follow rel=next in sync within a small budget (e.g. up to N pages, or until a page contains only unchanged items), or document that sync covers only the first page and show that in the sync message when a next link exists.
test_plan: Integration test: a 2-page feed where page 2 changes. Assert the change is applied (or, if kept as a documented limit, that the message mentions that only the first page was checked).
verification: 2026-10-01: tests/integration/hosting.php (explicit first-page scope, older episodes retained); docs/HOSTING.md. Regression reproduced before the repair and passed afterwards on the marked local test site.

title: HTTP 429/5xx reported as a wrong feed address; Retry-After ignored; back-off only after three failures
evidence:
includes/Hosting.php:583-596 at b1076c8: any non-200/304 status becomes "The feed address answered with HTTP status %d. Check the address in your host's dashboard."
Hosting.php:518-526: back-off only when failures >= 3, and the Retry-After header is never read.
reproduction:
`$S/wpq eval-file $S/sync-audit.php http`:
- HTTP 429: 'error / The feed address answered with HTTP status 429. Check the address in your host’s dashboard.' The same text for 500 and 503.
- Timeout: 'The feed could not be loaded: cURL error 28 …'.
- 12 simulated hourly cron runs against a 429 with 'Retry-After: 7200' fetched 'FFFF.F...F..': fetches at hours 0-3 regardless of Retry-After, then 1/2/4 h back-off as documented.
user_impact: Admins are told to check a correct address during a host outage or rate limit. The plugin keeps hitting a rate-limiting host every hour for the first 3 failures, contrary to Retry-After.
proposed_fix: Distinguish 404/410 (address), 401/403 (access), 429 (rate limited, honor Retry-After by storing a not-before time) and 5xx (temporary host problem) in the messages and the back-off.
test_plan: Integration test: 429 with Retry-After 7200, where the next scheduled run within 2 h does not fetch. Assert the messages per status class.
notes:
HTTP 429 Retry-After and 5xx backoff tests are pending.
Verification: tests/integration/audit-sync.php (first failure Retry-After, no early request, temporary 503; 1.3.0 baseline fails).

title: Signed/expiring enclosure URLs make every sync 'update' all episodes and store URLs that expire
evidence:
includes/Importer.php:170 $fingerprint = md5( wp_json_encode( $item ) ) and 206 comparison: any change of the signature query changes the fingerprint.
Importer.php:326 'audio_url' => esc_url_raw( item audio_url ) is stored verbatim.
Hosting.php:985-987 flushes the feed cache on every update.
user_impact: For hosts or CDNs that sign enclosure URLs per request: every hourly sync rewrites every episode and invalidates this site's feed cache and ETag, causing unnecessary load and 'N episodes updated' noise. The stored audio URL stops working when the signature expires.
proposed_fix: Compare enclosure URLs without volatile signature parameters (Expires, Signature, Key-Pair-Id, X-Amz-*, token …) when computing the fingerprint and field hashes. Warn the admin when the host's enclosure URLs are signed/expiring, since mirroring cannot keep them playable.
test_plan: Integration test: a signed-URL feed synced twice. Assert the second run reports 'Up to date.' and no post is modified.
notes: tests/integration/hosting.php (managed signed URLs refresh without edit timestamps or update counts; original raw hashes and local token-only edits are preserved; readiness warns about expiry)

title: Move after mirror leaves VTT/SRT caption files (and failed episode images) on the old host while summary, Readiness and docs imply a complete move

title: Media downloads have no size, disk, low-speed or rate-limit handling; a step can block 15 min and outlive the web request
evidence: includes/Importer.php:836 `$timeout = 'audio' === $kind ? 900 : 60;`, :843-844 `@set_time_limit( $timeout + 60 );`, :847 `$tmp = download_url( $url, $timeout );` (WP core download_url() streams to wp_tempnam() with no limit_response_size and no free-space check); no disk_free_space/size cap anywhere in includes/ (grep). ImportJob.php:482 `$batch = $download ? 1 : 10;` (one download per step, step holds the lock :471-475 and releases it only in finally :555-557). Feed side: Hosting.php:565 `'limit_response_size' => (int) apply_filters( 'epm_feed_max_bytes', 50 * MB_IN_BYTES )`, ImportJob.php:269 up to 50 pages (`epm_import_max_pages`). CHANGELOG.md:338-340 claims media downloads go through download_url 'with timeouts and size limits' — there is no size limit for media.
reproduction:
Local source: $S/mediaserver.py on 127.0.0.1:8962 (endpoints /len, /chunked, /close, /slow, /stall, /status/<code>, /html, /octet, /redirect, /feeds). Loopback allowed only in scratch code / a scratch mu-plugin via http_request_host_is_external + http_allowed_safe_ports for 127.0.0.1:8962 (the repo tests never open sockets: they answer download_url through pre_http_request in tests/fixtures/mu-plugins/epm-test-http.php:114-119).
- Size, no limit: `IMPB_URLS="http://127.0.0.1:8962/len/419430400/big400.mp3 http://127.0.0.1:8962/chunked/314572800/chunked300.mp3 http://127.0.0.1:8962/close/209715200/close200.mp3" /tmp/epm-a-import-b/wp eval-file $S/imp04-sideload.php` -> 400 MB attachment in 11.97 s, 300 MB chunked (no Content-Length) in 4.51 s, 200 MB close-delimited in 5.04 s; all stored as audio/mpeg (durations 29:07:38, 21:50:43, 14:33:49). Peak PHP memory 579.3 MB (see IMPB-N1).
- Stalled source (4 KB then silence): `IMPB_URLS=http://127.0.0.1:8962/stall/stall.mp3 ... imp04-sideload.php` -> 'seconds: 900.01', 'WP_Error http_request_failed: cURL error 28: Operation timed out after 900001 milliseconds with 4096 out of 10485760 bytes received'; server log 'CLIENT HUNG UP during stall after 900.0s'. No low-speed abort.
- Slow source behind nginx 1.24 + php-fpm 8.4 (defaults, fastcgi_read_timeout 60 s): `python3 $S/ajax-import.py http://localhost:8971 http://127.0.0.1:8962/feeds/slow-move.xml --copy` (3 MB at 40 KB/s) -> 'step 1: HTTP 504 60.0s' (nginx 'upstream timed out'), php-fpm access log 'POST /wp-admin/admin-ajax.php 200 77134.887 ms' — PHP kept going and copied s1.mp3; the UI (admin/js/epm-hosting.js:463-468) stops stepping and shows 'Something went wrong. Check your connection and try again. The import continues in the background if you leave this page.'
- HTTP errors / rate limits via AJAX (feed rate-limited.xml): r1,r2 429 with Retry-After: 3600 requested 0.5 s apart (no backoff), 'Audio stays on the host: Too Many Requests'; 404 -> 'Not Found'; all counted media_failed and listed. Temp files removed on these errors (new_tmp_files []).
- Catalog size: 5000 items / 10.3 MB feed via AJAX -> preview 0.7 s, 45 MB peak (fpm log), job file 11,030,561 bytes, every 10-item mirror step 2.3 s / 38 MB; json_decode of the job file alone 0.099 s / 32.5 MB per step.
user_impact: One slow or stalled host file blocks the import (and the lock, so syncs too) for up to 15 minutes per episode; a slow-but-alive host fails every file larger than 900 s × rate after wasting the full 15 min each; on common nginx/php-fpm stacks the browser gets a 504 and the progress UI stops although the server keeps working. Nothing caps a file's size or checks disk space, so a mislabeled or huge enclosure can fill the disk (see IMPB-N1/N2 for what happens then). A rate-limiting host (429) gets hammered with one request per step and every episode fails instead of the job pausing.
proposed_fix: Replace download_url() in Importer::sideload() with an own streamed wp_safe_remote_get (keeping reject_unsafe_urls + validated redirects): configurable caps per kind (filters, e.g. audio 1 GB, image 20 MB, transcript 5 MB) enforced while streaming (also without Content-Length) with explicit truncation detection; free-space check of temp dir and uploads against Content-Length/enclosure length + margin; low-speed abort (http_api_curl: CURLOPT_LOW_SPEED_LIMIT/TIME) and a per-request time budget well below 60 s with resumable Range downloads across steps (partial file tracked in the job) so AJAX/cron steps stay short behind proxies; honor 429/503 Retry-After by pausing the job (status 'waiting' until time) instead of failing items; per-item attempt counter and a final per-item failure reason. Keep one job framework.
test_plan: Integration tests with a local test server or pre_http_request streaming stubs: file above cap with and without Content-Length -> aborted, temp file removed, item reported with reason; stalled source -> aborted by low-speed limit within configured seconds; slow source larger than one step budget -> resumed across steps via Range, final file byte-identical; 429 with Retry-After -> job waits, no further requests before the time; 404/403/500 -> reported, retried on next run; free-space shortfall -> not attempted, reported. Measure with nginx+php-fpm defaults that no step exceeds 30 s.

title: Copying a large audio file exhausts PHP memory (core getimagesize on the audio via media_handle_sideload); job gets stuck, lock held, full-size orphan files accumulate
evidence: includes/Importer.php:886 `$attachment = media_handle_sideload( [ 'name' => $name, 'tmp_name' => $tmp ], $post_id, ... );` for every kind including audio. WP 7.1.2 media_handle_sideload() calls `wp_read_image_metadata( $file )` on any file, which calls wp_getimagesize() -> getimagesize() (wp-includes/media.php:5905). The file is already copied into uploads before that (wp_handle_sideload), and Importer.php:897 `wp_delete_file( $tmp );` only runs when media_handle_sideload returns a WP_Error, not on a fatal. After a fatal no `finally` runs (ImportJob.php:555-557) and no continuation is scheduled (schedule_continuation only at ImportJob.php:453/549/636).
reproduction:
Measured PHP 8.4.26: `php -d memory_limit=128M -r 'getimagesize("/tmp/impb-id3.mp3");'` on a 100 MB MP3 -> 'Allowed memory size of 134217728 bytes exhausted (tried to allocate 98569973 bytes)'; unlimited: getimagesize peak 192.0 MB for the 100 MB file; in WP ($S/imp04-memory2.php) the peak 321.3 MB for a 200 MB file occurs between wp_handle_sideload_overrides and wp_insert_attachment_data, i.e. in wp_read_image_metadata (wp_read_audio_metadata itself 76 MB). Web path, nginx+php-fpm defaults (memory_limit 128M; admin-ajax does not raise it): `python3 $S/ajax-import.py http://localhost:8963 http://127.0.0.1:8962/feeds/mem-move.xml --copy` -> 'step 1: HTTP 500 2.0s

There has been a critical error on this website.

'; php-fpm log 'PHP Fatal error: Allowed memory size of 134217728 bytes exhausted (tried to allocate 90180351 bytes) in .../wp-includes/media.php on line 5905'. State ($S/imp04-state.php): lock held, job running, position 0, episode 88 created without audio_id, _epm_copying set, orphan uploads/2026/06/m100.mp3 (104857600 bytes, no attachment). After the 20-min lock expiry the retry (WP-Cron on the php -S test server, 512M) copied it as m100-1.mp3; m100.mp3 stays orphaned (ls: m100.mp3 and m100-1.mp3, both 104857600). WP-Cron under php-fpm (cron raises to 256M), site /tmp/epm-a-import-b-3 with DISABLE_WP_CRON and `curl http://localhost:8971/wp-cron.php`: 240 MB item -> 'PHP Fatal error: Allowed memory size of 268435456 bytes exhausted (tried to allocate 232787709 bytes) in .../wp-includes/media.php on line 5905', fpm log 'GET /wp-cron.php 200 5083.348 ms 229 MB', orphan uploads/2026/06/p1.mp3 (251658240), lock held, job running at position 0, `cron_next: false` (no continuation scheduled).
user_impact: On typical hosts (128M web / 256M cron) moving a show with long episodes fails: the progress page shows a critical error, the job is stuck at the same item, every retry downloads the whole file again and leaves another full-size orphan in uploads (disk fills), files above roughly 200-230 MB can never be copied, and the background continuation is lost after a cron fatal so the job only moves when an admin reopens the page.
proposed_fix: Do not route audio through media_handle_sideload(): use wp_handle_sideload() + wp_insert_attachment() + wp_generate_attachment_metadata() (audio metadata only) so no image probe runs on audio; before downloading, record the item as in-progress in the job (attempt counter, target path) and register a shutdown handler that marks the item failed, deletes the partial/orphan file and schedules the continuation; skip an item after N failed attempts with a reported reason; reuse an existing orphan/attachment by _epm_source_url for audio too instead of creating -1 copies.
test_plan: Integration test that sideloads a generated audio file of e.g. 60 MB under ini_set('memory_limit', baseline+40M) and asserts success and bounded peak memory; fault-injection test that aborts after the file reached uploads (shutdown path) and asserts: no orphan file, lock released, item attempt counted, continuation scheduled, next run succeeds without a -1 duplicate; manual check with nginx+php-fpm defaults and a 300 MB file.

title: Full temp disk yields a truncated audio file that is stored as the episode's audio; full uploads leaves a partial file
evidence: includes/Importer.php:847 `$tmp = download_url( $url, $timeout );` — result is used without comparing the file size to Content-Length or the enclosure length, and without a free-space check; :759 `update_post_meta( $post_id, ...'audio_id', $attachment );` then makes the local file win over the working external URL (includes/Episodes.php:407-423 uses audio_url only when no attachment).
reproduction: Site /tmp/epm-a-import-b-2, 20 MB tmpfs as temp dir: `mount -t tmpfs -o size=20m tmpfs /tmp/impb-small-tmp; TMPDIR=/tmp/impb-small-tmp IMPB_KEEP=1 IMPB_URLS="http://127.0.0.1:8962/len/52428800/full1.mp3 http://127.0.0.1:8962/chunked/52428800/full2.mp3" /tmp/epm-a-import-b-2/wp eval-file $S/imp04-sideload.php` -> 54,566 notices 'fwrite(): Write of 1160 bytes failed with errno=28 No space left on device in .../Requests/src/Transport/Curl.php on line 556', then 'result: attachment 25', 'file_MB: 20', 'meta_length: 1:27:23' (source sent all 52428800 bytes) — same for the chunked variant (attachment 26, 20 MB). Uploads full (20 MB tmpfs mounted on uploads/2026/09): 'WP_Error upload_error: The uploaded file could not be moved to wp-content/uploads/2026/09.' and a partial full3.mp3 of 20971520 bytes left in that folder.
user_impact: A disk that runs full during a move silently replaces a working episode with a truncated copy (the feed's enclosure now points to the cut-off file, duration/size are taken from it) and reports success; a full uploads folder leaves partial files that nothing removes.
proposed_fix: After download verify bytes == Content-Length (when sent) and treat a mismatch, write errors or a size far below a plausible enclosure length as failure (delete temp, keep external URL, report reason); check disk_free_space() for temp and uploads before downloading; delete a partial target file when the move into uploads fails.
test_plan: Test with a small tmpfs (or a stub that truncates the stream): assert WP_Error, no attachment, temp removed, audio_url kept, reason listed; test uploads-full: assert no partial file remains in the month folder.

title: Process abort mid-copy: partial temp file stays, the episode being created loses chapters/transcripts permanently, CLI cannot cancel
evidence: includes/Importer.php:221-244: create() and write() run, then copy_media() (:231-237), and only afterwards fetch_chapters()/fetch_transcript() (:239-244); a later run takes the existing-episode branch (:172-219), which never fetches chapters or transcripts. download_url() leaves wp_tempnam() files on a killed process; nothing in the plugin cleans temp files. includes/Cli.php offers only import/status/sync; ImportJob::preview() refuses while status is running (ImportJob.php:241-244).
reproduction: Site /tmp/epm-a-import-b-2: `wp podcast import http://127.0.0.1:8962/feeds/kill-move.xml --move --copy-media --owner` (K1 = 60 MB at 1 MB/s with podcast:chapters + VTT, K2 small with the same chapters/VTT), `kill -9` after ~18 s. State: /tmp/k1-CrxLSQ.tmp 18979117 bytes left; lock held; job running, position 0; episode impb4k-1 published with external audio, 0 chapters, no transcript, _epm_copying set. Re-running the CLI: 'Error: An import is already running. Wait for it to finish or cancel it first.' (no CLI cancel; `wp podcast status` does not show the job). After the 20-min lock expiry `wp cron event run epm_import_continue` copied k1.mp3 ('updated'), then K2 was created with chapters 2, transcript text and transcript_file_id 31; a further `wp podcast import ... --move --copy-media --owner` -> 'Success: 0 new, 0 updated, 2 unchanged'; impb4k-1 still has chapters 0, transcript '' and no transcript file; /tmp/k1-CrxLSQ.tmp still present. (Checked and rejected along the way: a silent skip of the interrupted audio copy does not happen in this flow, because the 17-min _epm_copying marker expires before the 20-min lock.)
user_impact: A PHP-FPM request_terminate_timeout, OOM kill, deploy or Ctrl-C during a move silently drops the chapters and transcript of one episode for good, reports success on every later run, and leaves large partial files in the system temp dir; CLI users have no command to cancel the stuck job.
proposed_fix: Fetch chapters/transcripts before the media copy (or mark them pending and complete them for existing episodes when missing and importer-owned); keep temp downloads under a plugin prefix and delete stale ones on the next step; add `wp podcast import --cancel` (or `wp podcast cancel`) and show the job in `wp podcast status`.
test_plan: Fault injection (throw/exit inside the sideload for the first created item), then run the job again: assert chapters and transcript present for that episode, no stale temp file, client state reports the interrupted copy; CLI test for cancel and status output.

title: Downloaded content is not validated as audio: random octet-stream bytes become the episode MP3 and count as distribution-ready; HTML page gives a misleading error
evidence: includes/Importer.php:862-884: for an extension-less URL `$detected = (string) mime_content_type( $tmp );` and `$ext = $by_mime[ $detected ] ?? ( 'audio' === $kind ? 'mp3' : 'jpg' );` — unknown content defaults to .mp3; no check that the result is decodable audio or matches the enclosure type/length.
reproduction: Move via AJAX on /tmp/epm-a-import-b-3 (`python3 $S/ajax-import.py http://localhost:8971 http://127.0.0.1:8962/feeds/rate-limited.xml --copy`): item R4 (200000 random bytes, application/octet-stream, no extension) -> 'created | R4 octet | ' with no message, audio_id 31, file r4.mp3 200000 bytes; Readiness afterwards: 'ok | Distributable episodes | 10 episodes with distribution-ready audio.' title: Orphaned job files: concurrent previews and never-started previews leave job files indefinitely
evidence: includes/ImportJob.php:241 `$current = self::get();` read before the (slow) feed fetch, :262 `self::delete_file( $current );`, :355 `self::save( $job );` — two concurrent previews both delete the same old file and the later save wins, so the other new file is never referenced; `'created' => time()` (:353) is stored but never used for expiry; no cleanup of job-*.json other than delete_file() of the current job and uninstall.php:22-31.
reproduction: `/tmp/epm-a-import-b/wp eval-file $S/imp05-orphans.php` (sequential cases) then two concurrent previews: `IMPB_MODE=slowpreview IMPB_TAG=slowA IMPB_SLEEP=4 wp eval-file $S/imp05-orphans.php &` and 1.5 s later `IMPB_MODE=slowpreview IMPB_TAG=fastB IMPB_SLEEP=0 ...` -> '[fastB] ... files now=["job-NXVb8iZNGYfOnoXsMNHGQziW.json"]', '[slowA] ... files now=["job-NXVb8i...json","job-zqBNg5...json"]', job token = zqBNg5...; after ImportJob::cancel(): 'after cancel: job-NXVb8iZNGYfOnoXsMNHGQziW.json' (still there; served by nginx per IMP-05). Reproduced again on /tmp/epm-a-import-b-3 (job-av6kjs... and job-g0ZYcG...). Sequential cases OK: cancel -> file deleted; second preview -> old deleted; failing preview -> the still-valid ready job and its file kept; done -> deleted; missing data -> status failed. Never-started preview (case e): job keeps 'created', nothing expires it. After a fatal step (IMPB-N1) the file stays with a 'running' job until cancel. Uninstall simulation ($S/imp05-uninstall.php on site 3) removed the folder including both orphans and the import options.
user_impact: Two admins or two tabs checking a feed at the same time, or a preview that is never started, leave parsed-feed files in uploads indefinitely (publicly readable on nginx, see IMP-05) until the plugin is uninstalled.
proposed_fix: Make preview atomic (take the import lock or compare-and-swap the job option) and, after saving, delete every job file that is not the current job's; expire 'ready' jobs after e.g. 24 h (daily cleanup or on next admin load) and remove files older than that; on multisite, clean every site's folder on uninstall (untested here).
test_plan: Integration test: two previews with an interleaving hook (sleep inside a route) -> exactly one job file afterwards; ready job older than the TTL -> file and job removed by the cleanup; cancel/replace/done/uninstall assertions kept.

title: Elementor element_ready hooks registered without the skin suffix never fire; widgets initialize only through the MutationObserver fallback
evidence:
assets/js/epm-player.js:1816-1822 at b1076c8:
  ['epm-podcast-player', 'epm-episode-list', 'epm-latest-episode', 'epm-chapters', 'epm-episode-video'].forEach(function (widgetName) {
    frontend.hooks.addAction(
      'frontend/element_ready/' + widgetName, ...
Elementor 4.3.3 (vendor, /tmp/epm-a-player/site/wp-content/plugins/elementor/assets/js/frontend.js:3769-3773) fires only 'frontend/element_ready/global', '.../widget' and `frontend/element_ready/${$scope.attr("data-widget_type")}`. The rendered attribute is data-widget_type="epm-podcast-player.default" (all 11 widgets on /epm-elementor/ end in .default). Official docs (https://developers.elementor.com/add-javascript-to-elementor-widgets/, read 2026-09-30) use "frontend/element_ready/your-widget-name.default". The fallback that masks this is epm-player.js:1835-1874 (MutationObserver -> init(node)). The docs claim otherwise: CHANGELOG.md:471 ("idempotent per-widget Elementor init") and CHANGELOG.md:406-407. tests/e2e/run.mjs:169-170 ('players initialize in the editor preview') passes only through the observer.
reproduction:
The test copy of epm-player.js is served via context.route (the repo is not edited). It is instrumented to count hook callbacks and init() calls. Variants: observer on/off, hooks with/without .default.

1) `node play01-frontend.mjs` on /epm-elementor/:
- Repo code: 'EPM hook callbacks run :: []' although Elementor fired element_ready for all 11 "epm-*.default" types.
- Observer OFF, no suffix: a late widget run through elementorFrontend.elementsHandler.runReadyTrigger(el) gives 'FAIL late-inserted widget initialized :: {"init":[],"hook":[],"initialized":false}'.
- Observer OFF + .default: 'EPM hook callbacks run :: ["epm-podcast-player","epm-episode-list","epm-latest-episode","epm-chapters"]' and the late widget initializes.

2) `node play01-editor.mjs repo obs-off obs-off+suffix obs-on+suffix`, in the real Elementor editor, using $e commands document/elements/create, settings, duplicate, delete, document/history/undo and redo, then 10 layout re-renders:
- repo: all PASS with hookCalls 0 and initCalls 20. One click listener per play button; one click gives plays=1, pauses=0.
- obs-off: 'FAIL initial players initialized :: [{"id":"12","init":false,"clicks":0},{"id":"16","init":false,...}]'. Insert, switch, duplicate, undo and the re-renders all show init:false and clicks:0. 'one click = one playback :: {"controller":false}'.
- obs-off+suffix: all PASS, hookCalls 19.
- obs-on+suffix: all PASS, no duplicate listeners ([1,1,1,1]).

The results reproduced after a reseed (out-play01-*.rerun.txt).
user_impact: No visible failure today in Elementor 4.3.3 / Chromium: the observer initializes everything. The documented per-widget Elementor path is dead code, though. Initialization in the editor depends entirely on the observer, and the docs and tests claim a hook path that does not work. If the observer is removed, throttled, or the DOM is inserted in a way it misses, every widget in the editor stays dead (reproduced with the observer off).
proposed_fix: Register 'frontend/element_ready/' + widgetName + '.default'. For robustness against custom skins, instead add one 'frontend/element_ready/widget' handler that checks $scope.attr('data-widget_type') against /^epm-(podcast-player|episode-list|latest-episode|chapters|episode-video)\./. Keep the MutationObserver as a documented fallback and keep init() idempotent. Correct CHANGELOG.md and TEST-PLAN.md.
test_plan: Add an e2e suite based on play01-editor.mjs that serves the engine with the observer disabled through page.route. Assert initialization through hooks alone for: initial render, insert, switch episode, duplicate, delete, undo/redo, 10 re-renders. With both paths on, assert one click listener per control and one click giving exactly one play event. On the frontend, call runReadyTrigger on a late widget with the observer off.
notes: Elementor Pro Theme Builder, Loop Grid/Carousel and Popups were not testable (no Pro license on the site). The DOM they insert is covered by the observer; see PLAY-N1 for cloned DOM. The widgets register no skins, so '.default' is always the suffix.

title: Controller keyed only by episode ID: a changed source is never adopted (old audio plays, fixed source stays in error), metadata goes stale, removed views are retained
evidence:
assets/js/epm-player.js at b1076c8:
- Lines 588-601 (Registry.get): `var controller = this.controllers[id]; if (!controller && typeof factory === 'function') { controller = factory(); ...}`. There is no source comparison.
- Lines 889-897 (bindFullPlayer): `Registry.get(episodeId, function () { return new PlaybackController(episodeId, audio, {title..., artwork..., duration...}); })`. A later view's own <audio> and data-epm-src/title/duration are ignored.
- Card buttons (1030-1040) and chapters (1069-1079) behave the same way.
- Retry (493-500) calls audio.load() on the same stale element.
- Stale metadata shows in Sticky.attach (1269-1278) and MediaSession (659-665).
- getDuration (558-565) prefers the old element's duration.
- Views are pruned only inside _emit (439-451); subscribe() (421-431) never prunes; controllers are never removed from Registry.
reproduction:
1) `node play02-frontend.mjs` (frontend, /epm-elementor/): play ep1 (A = epm-episode-1.mp3), pause, then replace the player widget's markup with the same episode ID and audio B (epm-episode-2.mp3) and press play. Output:
'after re-render with B + play :: {"controllerSrc":".../epm-episode-1.mp3","controllerAudioIsNewElement":false,"newAudioElementSrc":".../epm-episode-2.mp3","duration":95.004,...,"stickyTitle":"Episode One: Hello & “Friends”","metaTitle":"Episode One...","mediaSessionTitle":"Episode One..."}'
Result: FAIL, audio A plays and the title is stale.

2) Error case: A answers 404 through a route; press play (error on the player, sticky and Retry). Re-render with a working B, press play. Output: 'controllerSrc: .../epm-episode-1.mp3 ... "error":true,"uiError":true, stickyTitle "This audio could not be loaded."'. The fixed source is never tried.

3) `node play02-editor.mjs` (real editor): play and pause ep1, then `update_post_meta(ep1,'_epm_audio_id',audio_2)` via wp-cli, then re-render the widget with a layout change and press play. Output: '{"markupSrc":".../epm-episode-2.mp3","ownAudio":".../epm-episode-2.mp3","playing":".../epm-episode-1.mp3","duration":95.004}'. FAIL. The meta was restored afterwards.

4) 40 re-renders of a paused player: 'before {"views":2} after {"views":42,"connectedViews":2}'. After one seek event: {"views":2}.

5) Editor run (play01-editor repo): after switching the widget from ep13 to ep14, the controller for 13 stays registered with its detached audio ('final controllers' lists 12, 13, 14, 16, all with audioConnected false except 16). Growth is bounded by the number of distinct episode IDs.

The results reproduced after a reseed.
user_impact: When an editor replaces an episode's audio file (or fixes a broken URL) while the Elementor editor is open, the preview keeps playing the old file or keeps showing 'could not be loaded' until a full reload. The same happens for any dynamic re-render on the frontend. The duration, sticky title and lock-screen title stay stale. Detached DOM trees accumulate on paused episodes during long editor sessions.
proposed_fix:
Give the controller a source identity:
- On every bind (full player, card, chapters), compare the view's data-epm-src with controller.src.
- On a real change: pause, set audio.src to the new URL, reset _restored/_pendingSeek/error, load(), and emit 'attach'/'loaded' so views, the sticky bar and MediaSession refresh.
- When the source is the same, keep playback, including while it is playing.
- Refresh meta (title, artwork, duration) from the newest connected view.
- Prune disconnected views in subscribe() as well as in _emit.
- Drop controllers with no connected view that are not active or playing.
notes: Card and chapter views for the same episode stay in sync with the (stale) controller. The problem is which source the shared controller uses, not the sync between views.

title: Re-rendering the widget whose <audio> the controller adopted pauses playback (Elementor control change, DOM replacement)
evidence: assets/js/epm-player.js:870 `var audio = root.querySelector('audio');` and 891-892 `Registry.get(episodeId, function () { return new PlaybackController(episodeId, audio, {...` The shared controller adopts the <audio> element inside the first full player's DOM. When that DOM leaves the document, the browser runs the media-element removal steps (internal pause), so re-rendering that one view stops playback for every view of the episode. The brief's PLAY-02 order asks to keep intentionally playing audio across a harmless layout re-render.
reproduction:
`node play02-editor-remove.mjs` (real editor, page with two ep1 player widgets and no sticky bar): play widget 1, then change its layout through $e. Output:
'playing :: {"playing":true,...}'
'after re-render while playing :: {"playing":false,"t":1.2,"uiPlaying":[false,false]}'
Result: FAIL.

`node play02-detach.mjs` (frontend /audit-two-players/): replacing the second, non-owning player keeps playing ('{"replaced":1,"ownerIndex":0,"playing":true,"pauseEvents":0}'). Replacing the owning player pauses ('{"replaced":0,"ownerIndex":0,"playing":false,"pauseEvents":1}').

The results reproduced after a reseed.
user_impact: In the Elementor editor, adjusting any control of the player that is playing stops the audio. On the frontend, any script that re-renders the first player (AJAX refresh, page transitions) stops playback. Both are unexpected, and the only remedy is to press play again.
proposed_fix: Let every controller own a detached Audio element (makeAudio(src)), as cards and chapters already do. The rendered <audio> stays only as the no-JS/fallback element: set its preload to none, or remove its src once bound, so the page does not fetch metadata twice. Alternatively, move the adopted element into a hidden container attached to <body> before binding.
test_plan: Use play02-detach.mjs as a regression test: replacing either view while playing keeps isPlaying() true and the new view shows is-playing. In an editor e2e test, change a control on the playing widget and assert that playback continues.
notes: Removing every view of a playing episode also stops the audio in the editor (it was paused by the same mechanism). That outcome is acceptable, but it happens by accident rather than by design.

title: Volume and mute are not propagated between views, native volume changes are ignored, and the slider does nothing on iOS
evidence: assets/js/epm-player.js:550-556 (setVolume only sets `this.audio.volume = Math.min(1, Math.max(0, v));`, emits no event and never touches muted). Lines 924-929 bind the input listener and set `refs.volume.value = String(controller.audio.volume);` once at bind time. _attachAudioEvents (359-387) has no 'volumechange' listener, and updatePlayerUI (761-812) never updates refs.volume. includes/Renderer.php:1202-1205 renders <input type=range ... data-epm-volume aria-label="Volume"> with no aria-valuetext and no mute control. Apple: "On iOS devices, the audio level is always under the user's physical control. The volume property is not settable in JavaScript. Reading the volume property always returns 1." (https://developer.apple.com/library/archive/documentation/AudioVideo/Conceptual/Using_HTML5_Audio_Video/Device-SpecificConsiderations/Device-SpecificConsiderations.html, read 2026-09-30).
reproduction:
`node play03.mjs` on /audit-two-players/ (two full players of ep1; one shared controller that uses player A's <audio>):
- 6x ArrowLeft on slider A: '{"sliders":["0.7","1"],"audioVolume":0.7}', so 'FAIL slider B shows the same volume as slider A'.
- Click at the left end of A: '["0","1"]', audioVolume 0, muted false.
- Native `audio.volume=0.3; audio.muted=true`: sliders stay '["0","1"]' (FAIL).
- A third player bound later picks up 0.3 (init only).
- After a reload the volume is back to 1 (not persisted).
- The mute control count in the markup is 0.

The results reproduced after a reseed.
user_impact: On pages with two views of one episode (for example an automatic episode page player plus a player widget), the second slider shows the wrong level, and touching it makes the volume jump. A mute set by another script or device is invisible, and moving the slider does not unmute. On iPhone/iPad every full player shows a volume slider that has no effect.
proposed_fix:
- Listen to 'volumechange' in _attachAudioEvents and emit 'volume'.
- In updatePlayerUI set refs.volume.value = audio.muted ? 0 : audio.volume. A programmatic value does not fire 'input', so this cannot loop.
- setVolume(v > 0) clears muted.
- Add aria-valuetext as a percentage.
- Detect a read-only volume once (set 0.5 and read it back). If it cannot be set, hide the slider (class on the root) and rely on the device volume. Optionally persist the volume like the speed.
notes: The iOS behavior is documented by Apple, not reproduced here: no iOS device or Safari was available, and WebKit automation is not iOS Safari.

title: Cloned DOM (e.g. Swiper loop duplicates) copies data-epm-initialized / -card-bound / -chapters-bound / -share-bound, so clones are never bound and their buttons are dead
evidence: assets/js/epm-player.js at b1076c8 treats a data attribute as proof of binding: 867 `if (!root || root.nodeType !== 1 || root.dataset.epmInitialized) { return; }`, 1017 `btn.dataset.epmCardBound`, 1052 `container.dataset.epmChaptersBound`, 1387 `root.dataset.epmShareBound`, 1716 `root.dataset.epmVideoBound`. cloneNode(true) copies these attributes but not the listeners. Elementor 4.3.3 bundles Swiper 8.4.5 (assets/lib/swiper/v8/swiper.js:3154/3158: `$selector.append($(appendSlides[i].cloneNode(true)).addClass(params.slideDuplicateClass))`).
reproduction:
`node clone-swiper.mjs` on /audit-two-players/: the page loads normally (cards bound), then Elementor's own swiper.js v8 is loaded and three bound episode cards are put into `new Swiper(el, {loop:true})`. Output:
'swiper loop duplicate card button :: {"duplicates":2,"flagCopied":"1","clickListeners":0,"controllerAfterClick":false,"playing":false}'
Result: FAIL, a click on a duplicated card does nothing. The MutationObserver sees the clones, but init() skips them because of the copied flags. Reproduced after a reseed.
user_impact: In carousels that loop by cloning slides, some slides' play, share and chapter controls do nothing. Elementor Pro's Loop Carousel with loop enabled is the likely path. The only workaround is to disable looping.
proposed_fix: Track bound elements in a module-level WeakSet (or WeakMap element -> binding) instead of trusting data attributes: `if (bound.has(root)) return; bound.add(root);`. Clones are not in the set and get bound. Keep the data attribute only as a debugging marker, or strip it from clones.
test_plan: Use clone-swiper.mjs as a regression test: each duplicated card, player and chapter list must have exactly one click listener, and a click must play. Idempotence tests (init(document) run 3x plus observer plus hooks) must still show one listener per control.
notes: Mechanism reproduced with the real Swiper 8.4.5 that Elementor ships. The Elementor Pro Loop Carousel path itself was not tested (no Pro license), so the Pro user impact is inferred.

title: Preferred speed is not applied to controllers that already exist (another episode's player on the page)
evidence: assets/js/epm-player.js:280-287 (the stored speed is read only in the PlaybackController constructor) and 542-548 (cycleSpeed changes only this controller and stores 'speed'). Full players create their controllers at page init, so a later change never reaches them.
reproduction: `node speed-carry.mjs` on /epm-elementor/: set 1.25x on the ep1 player, then press play on the latest-episode player. Output: '{"stored":"1.25","aLabel":"1.25×","bLabel":"1×","bRate":1,"stickySpeed":"1×"}'. FAIL.
user_impact: The code comment says the preferred speed carries over between episodes, but that only happens after a reload or for lazily created controllers. The next episode on the same page plays at 1x.
proposed_fix: On cycleSpeed, apply the rate to all registered controllers, or read Store 'speed' in play() before starting. Emit 'speed' so their views update.
test_plan: speed-carry.mjs: after changing the speed on A and playing B, B's playbackRate, label and the sticky label all equal the stored speed.

title: Opening a ?t= link (without playing) overwrites the visitor's remembered resume position
evidence: assets/js/epm-player.js:394-408 (cue() sets _restored and either seeks or sets _pendingSeek). 363-370 applies the pending seek on loadedmetadata, which fires timeupdate. 352-356 `_remember`: `if (eventName === 'pause' || (eventName === 'time' && Math.abs(t - this._lastSaved) >= 5)) { ... Store.set('pos:' + this.episodeId, ...)`. A cue is not playback, but it is saved as a position.
reproduction: `node acceptance-1.mjs`, section 3, on the self-hosted episode page: set localStorage epm:pos:<id>=40, then open ?t=20 without pressing play. Output: 'stored 40 + ?t=20 (not played) :: {"t":20,...,"stored":"20"}'. Reloading without ?t= then starts at 20 ('reload without ?t= after that :: {"t":20 ...}'). The same effect occurs with a seek before playing (for example keyboard +10 s stores 10).
user_impact: A listener who half-finished an episode and clicks a shared timestamp link loses their own place, even if they never play from the link.
proposed_fix: Save positions only after playback has started for that controller (a played flag set on 'play'), or ignore 'time' events caused by cue() or an initial restore.
test_plan: acceptance-1.mjs section 3: after opening ?t=20 without play, the stored position stays 40; after playing past 25 s it updates.

title: Out-of-range or huge ?t= values are clamped to the last second (play ends immediately); with unknown duration the UI shows e.g. 'Starts at 27:46:39'
evidence: assets/js/epm-player.js:168-188 (parseTimestamp accepts any value up to 16 characters, e.g. '99999999', '10000h') and 394-399 (`if (d > 0) { t = Math.min(t, Math.max(0, Math.floor(d) - 1)); }`). With d = 0 the value is not bounded, and cueHint (1663-1673) prints it.
reproduction:
`node acceptance-1.mjs`, section 2:
- ep1 (95 s) with t=99999999, 9999999999999999, 10000h or 94.9: before play 'Starts at 1:34', after play '{"t":95,"paused":true,"ended":true}'.
- External episode without duration, t=99999: before play current '27:46:39', total '0:00', label 'Play episode, Starts at 27:46:39'; after play ended at 62.03.
- Valid forms (1m5s, 65, 1:05) cue at 1:05 and invalid ones (-5, abc, 1:99, 1e3, 0) are ignored, as intended.
user_impact: A malformed or stale timestamp link makes play look broken: about one second of audio, then 'ended'. With unknown duration the player shows a nonsensical position.
proposed_fix: Treat t >= duration as invalid (start at 0, or ignore). When the duration is unknown, keep the pending seek but validate it on loadedmetadata (drop it if >= duration), and do not show the hint above a sane cap.
test_plan: acceptance-1.mjs section 2 cases: out-of-range values start at 0 with no 'Starts at' hint; valid values stay unchanged.

title: MediaSession position state is not updated after seeks
evidence: assets/js/epm-player.js:670-678: setPositionState is only called for eventName 'loaded' | 'speed' | 'play' | 'pause'. seekAbsolute (522-536) emits 'time', which is ignored here.
reproduction: `node acceptance-2.mjs`, section 7 (setActionHandler/setPositionState wrapped by an init script): the handlers work (seekforward +30, seekbackward -10, seekto 70), but 'positionUpdatesAfterSeek: 0' and 'lastPosition {"duration":95.004,"playbackRate":1,"position":1.088}' after seeking to 70. FAIL.
user_impact: Lock-screen and OS media controls show the wrong elapsed time after any seek (in-page timeline, chapters, or the media keys themselves) until the next play or pause.
proposed_fix: Call setPositionState on 'seeked' (add a 'seeked' -> 'time' mapping or a dedicated event) and after seekAbsolute, throttled.
test_plan: acceptance-2.mjs section 7: position state count increases after each seek, and the last position equals currentTime.

title: Seek slider (role=slider) ignores ArrowUp/ArrowDown; the page scrolls instead
evidence: assets/js/epm-player.js:696-723 (sliderKeys handles ArrowLeft/Right, PageUp/Down, Home/End only). The WAI-ARIA APG slider pattern also maps Up/Down to increase/decrease.
reproduction: `node acceptance-3.mjs`, section 9: with the timeline focused, ArrowUp leaves t at 5.6 and scrollY changes 596 -> 594. 'FAIL ArrowUp on the slider seeks forward (APG slider) instead of scrolling'.
user_impact: Screen-reader and keyboard users who expect Up/Down on a slider scroll the page instead of seeking.
proposed_fix: Map ArrowUp to +5 and ArrowDown to -5 in sliderKeys, with preventDefault.
test_plan: Keyboard e2e: Up/Down change aria-valuenow and do not change scrollY, for both the player and the sticky timeline.

title: Sticky bar ignores left/right safe-area insets (landscape notch with viewport-fit=cover)
evidence: assets/css/epm-frontend.css:1372 `padding: 10px 20px calc(10px + env(safe-area-inset-bottom, 0px));` Only the bottom inset is used.
reproduction: `node acceptance-3.mjs`, section 12: 844x390 mobile context, CDP Emulation.setSafeAreaInsetsOverride {left:47,right:47,bottom:21}, with and without an injected viewport-fit=cover. Output: 'sticky {paddingLeft 20px, paddingRight 20px, paddingBottom 31px, height 87}', artworkLeft 20, closeRight 20. The bottom inset works (PASS). Left/right: FAIL. Screenshot: out/safe-area-cover-true.png.
user_impact: On notched phones in landscape, with a theme that sets viewport-fit=cover, the artwork and close button sit under the notch or rounded corner.
proposed_fix: padding-inline: max(20px, env(safe-area-inset-left)) max(20px, env(safe-area-inset-right)), or padding-left/right calc(20px + env(...)).
test_plan: acceptance-3.mjs section 12: artworkLeft >= 47 and closeRight >= 47 with the override; no change without insets.
notes: Emulated in Chromium through CDP. Chromium applies the override even without viewport-fit=cover, while real iOS exposes the insets only with cover. Not verified on a real iPhone.

title: Volume slider accessibility and touch size; seek slider touch target below 24 px
evidence: includes/Renderer.php:1203-1204 (`<input type="range" min="0" max="1" step="0.05" value="1" data-epm-volume aria-label="Volume" />`: no aria-valuetext, so it is spoken as 0.95). assets/css/epm-frontend.css:501-509 (width 80px, 56px at <=768px) and 414-419 (.epm-player__timeline height: 20px). The coarse-pointer block (2048-2060) does not enlarge either.
reproduction: `node acceptance-3.mjs`, sections 9 and 10: 'volume slider exposes :: {"valuetext":null,"value":"0.95"}'. Touch target sizes at 390 px: player play 56x56, skips 47x44, timeline 320x20, speed 44x44, volume 56x16, share 87x44; sticky play/speed/close 44x44, sticky timeline 390x24.
user_impact: The volume is announced as a bare fraction, and the volume and seek sliders are small to hit on touch screens (below WCAG 2.2 AA 2.5.8's 24 px).
proposed_fix: Set aria-valuetext as a percentage on input. Under (pointer: coarse) raise the timeline and volume hit areas to at least 24 px (padding or a pseudo-element), without changing the visual track.
test_plan: Touch e2e at 390 px: bounding boxes of timeline and volume are at least 24 px high; aria-valuetext reads e.g. '95%'.

title: Sticky.init latches 'initialized' without a shell: enabling the sticky player in the editor (or a shell inserted later) never works until reload
evidence: assets/js/epm-player.js:1103-1113: `if (this.initialized) { return; } this.initialized = true; var root = document.querySelector('[data-epm-sticky]'); if (!root) { return; }`. The shell is printed only in wp_footer when a render requested it (includes/Assets.php maybe_output_sticky), so re-rendering a widget with AJAX in the editor never adds it.
reproduction: `node misc.mjs`, part A (real editor, page without sticky): set sticky=yes on widget a0d17c1 via $e, wait for the re-render, press play. Output: '{"shell":false,"visible":false,"stickyInitialized":true,"stickyRoot":false}'. FAIL.
user_impact: In the editor preview, turning on the widget's 'Sticky player' shows nothing until the page is saved and reloaded, which looks broken. A shell inserted later by a script is never bound either.
proposed_fix: Mark Sticky initialized only once a root was found, and retry in init(scope). Optionally print the shell (hidden) in the Elementor preview whenever any EPM player widget is present.
test_plan: Editor e2e: enable sticky on a widget in a page without it; after play the sticky bar is visible, or the control says 'visible after reload' if that is chosen as the behavior.

title: Controller metadata depends on which view created it; chapter-first playback has no artwork (sticky bar, lock screen)
evidence: includes/Renderer.php:454 (the chapters container carries data-epm-episode-id/src/title but no artwork or duration). assets/js/epm-player.js:1074-1078 (`new PlaybackController(episodeId, makeAudio(src), { title: ..., artwork: '', duration: 0 })`). A later card of the same episode reuses this controller (Registry.get).
user_impact: The sticky bar and the lock screen show no cover art when playback starts from a chapter list.

title: Internal-entity amplification (quadratic blowup) in FeedParser: a ~100 KB feed expands to 500 MB, ties up a PHP worker for minutes; in WP-Cron sync it fatals without recording a failure and leaves the import lock
evidence: includes/FeedParser.php:172 `$doc = simplexml_load_string( $xml, \SimpleXMLElement::class, LIBXML_NOCDATA | LIBXML_NONET | LIBXML_COMPACT );`: an internal DTD subset is accepted and entity references are expanded when cast to string. includes/FeedParser.php:484 `$title = $this->plain( (string) $i->title );` (the fatal error points here). The docblock at FeedParser.php:13-15 claims 'entity expansion stays bounded … libxml's amplification guard rejects "billion laughs"'. That holds for nested entities but not for one large entity referenced many times on libxml 2.9.14 (LIBXML_DOTTED_VERSION on this PHP 8.4.26). Sync path: Hosting.php:806 acquires the lock and Hosting.php:852 parses. update_state() only runs after the parse returns, so a fatal error records nothing.
reproduction:
Fixtures are in scratch feeds/ and served from the site as http://localhost:8926/audit/…
1) `wp eval-file p/xml_parse.php feeds` (CLI, memory_limit -1): `quadratic.xml 141.992s peak+1430.5MB parsed: … item0 title len=500000005`. The rerun gave 146.6 s. quadratic.xml is 115,323 bytes: one 100,000-byte internal entity referenced 5,000 times. In the same run: xxe.xml gives title 'XXE end' (the file entity is not resolved); xxe-dtd.xml makes no request to the 127.0.0.1:8966 listener; billion.xml gives the literal 'BL &l9;'; invalid.xml gives WP_Error epm_feed_invalid.
2) AJAX epm_import_preview as admin, url=http://localhost:8926/audit/quadratic.xml: the client got 'Remote end closed connection without response'. server.log: `Fatal error: Maximum execution time of 30+2 seconds exceeded (terminated) in /home/user/elementor-podcast-manager/includes/FeedParser.php on line 484`, about 10 min after the request (05:16 to 05:26).
3) 53 KB variant (quadratic-50m.xml), `python3 p/quad_ajax.py p http://localhost:8926/audit/quadratic-50m.xml`: success in 3.5 s, maximum PHP RSS 232 MB. It wrote `job-PEHKnKNrKFSxds8RKtWka17E.json` of 50,000,368 bytes to uploads/epm-import.
4) Real WP-Cron sync: epm_hosting mode=external, feed_url=http://localhost:8926/audit/quadratic-300m.xml (109 KB), epm_sync_feed scheduled as due, then GET /wp-cron.php. The worker died with the same fatal error at FeedParser.php line 484; PHP RSS peaked at 310 MB within 25 s. Afterwards epm_sync_state showed `failures=0 last_run=0 status=` and `epm_import_lock = '1790832925:KNdU1bdPmvl0'` was still set. The next sync was scheduled in 3593 s. Two of the four php -S workers were killed by the hard timeout and not respawned (5 to 3 processes).
proposed_fix:
Before calling simplexml, reject any document that has an internal DTD subset or an ENTITY declaration (podcast RSS never needs one). For example: if `preg_match('/<!DOCTYPE[^>]*\[/i', $head) || stripos($xml, '<!ENTITY') !== false`, return a WP_Error ("The feed declares XML entities, which podcast feeds never use"). Alternatively, strip the DOCTYPE before loading. Also:
- Cap field lengths in the parser (title/summary to a few KB, HTML notes to about 1 MB) and the total size of the job file.
- In Hosting::sync, update last_run and failures before fetching, or register a shutdown handler that records the fatal error and releases the lock (this ties in with IMP-02 and SYNC-N4).
test_plan:
Integration tests:
- parse(quadratic fixture) returns a WP_Error within 1 s and grows memory by less than 10 MB.
- Billion-laughs and XXE fixtures stay rejected or inert.
- A normal feed that has an empty DOCTYPE still parses.
- A sync against the quadratic fixture counts one failure, writes last_run and leaves no epm_import_lock.
- HTTP check: an AJAX preview of the fixture answers in under 2 s with an error message.
notes:
DTD rejection and feed size cap are implemented; parser runtime stress coverage is pending.
Verification: tests/integration/hosting.php (DTD rejected before expansion; original parser accepts the small reproducer).

title: FeedParser::plain() truncates imported text at a literal '<' followed by a non-space (titles, summaries, channel/author names)

"C++ <templates> explained" => "C++ explained"
"<< Rewind" => "" (empty)

title: An https feed that redirects to http is fetched and imported over plain HTTP; only the permanent-move adoption is refused
evidence: includes/Hosting.php:558-567 `wp_safe_remote_get( $url, [ … 'redirection' => 5, … ] )` follows every redirect. reproduction:

1. $S/perf/generate.php 1000 40 created 1000 published episodes, each with a 40 KB _epm_transcript (39.1 MB in total); dump saved as perf/epm_perf-1000-transcripts40k.sql.gz.
2. perf/upgrade-outage.sh sets wp_options.epm_version='1.2.0' through SQL (simulating an update without loading WordPress) and requests /, /podcast/feed/, /wp-login.php and /wp-admin/ three times.

Hosting::unschedule_all() (Hosting.php:502-506) clears epm_import_continue on deactivation. Activation (elementor-podcast-manager.php:68-80) and Hosting::ensure_schedule() (Hosting.php:491-495) restore only the sync event.

ImportJob::preview() refuses while status is 'running' (ImportJob.php:241-244).

Only admin/js/epm-hosting.js:559-563 resumes stepping when the page loads with job.status running.
reproduction:
/tmp/epm-a-life-perf-qa, life/jobstate.php around each step.

Plain sequence:
- before: job running 10/60, file present, cron [sync, ping, import_continue]
- after deactivate: job running 10/60, file kept, cron []
- after activate: job running 10/60, cron [epm_sync_feed] only
- wp cron event run --due-now: 0 events, still 10/60
- ImportJob::preview(buzzsprout) -> 'An import is already running. Wait for it to finish or cancel it first.'

Race, with DISABLE_WP_CRON set temporarily: life/slow-step.php (1 s per created episode) ran in the background while wp plugin deactivate ran. The step finished at 16/60, released the lock and wrote no new cron event.

Resuming after reactivation by stepping (what the Hosting screen does): done 60/60, counts created 60, 60 episodes with 60 distinct GUIDs (no duplicates, no loss).
user_impact: After a deactivate/reactivate (for example while troubleshooting), the import silently stops. The setup assistant and other screens refuse to check a new feed until the user opens Podcast → Hosting & import, where it resumes, or cancels. No data loss.
proposed_fix: On activation (or init) reschedule epm_import_continue when the stored job is 'running'. Surface a notice on plugin screens for a paused import.
test_plan: Integration test: running job → deactivate hook → activate hook. Assert epm_import_continue is scheduled and run_in_background() continues to done without duplicate GUIDs.
notes: tests/integration/audit-sync.php (deactivation/reactivation restores one continuation event and retains progress; stopped jobs stay stopped; original activation fails)

title: Delete-mode uninstall deletes episodes one by one: 74 s and 201k queries for 5000 episodes; from the web the request gets a 504
evidence: uninstall.php:62-73: get_posts( ... 'posts_per_page' => -1 ... ) then wp_delete_post( $epm_episode_id, true ) for every episode in one request. Options are deleted before the episodes (uninstall.php:44-55), so an interrupted run leaves episodes without settings.
reproduction:
MariaDB perf site, 5000 episodes.

CLI: 'delete-mode uninstall of 5000 episodes (MariaDB, CLI, no time limit): 74.1 s, 201050 queries, peak 82.9 MB' (perf/uninstall-5000.txt).

Through nginx and php-fpm (perf/audit-uninstall-web.php calling uninstall_plugin() in a php-fpm request; plugin files not deleted): client got 'HTTP 504 after 60.06s'. PHP kept running ('shutdown after 78.4 s wall, max_execution_time=30, error=null, episodes left=0'). max_execution_time counts CPU time only on Linux.
user_impact: A site owner deleting the plugin with 'delete all data' sees a gateway timeout. On hosts that kill long requests (request_terminate_timeout, proxies), deletion stops partway: settings are gone and episodes are half deleted.
