Bulk uninstall passes 14 assertions on the marked MariaDB 11.4 network: 5,000 episodes removed in 0.55s with 686 queries. Revisions/comments and their metadata removed; attachments retained and detached. A database delete failure preserves settings and allows retry. CLI timing measured; php-fpm timing not yet run.

title: Import step overhead: feed-cache flush on every meta write, the whole job file decoded per step, a GUID map rebuilt per step, and an N+1 for the import log on every plugin screen
evidence:
Per-step costs in ImportJob::step():
- Feed.php:94-96: added/updated/deleted_post_meta call maybe_flush_on_meta, which runs Feed::flush_cache() (delete_transient) for every _epm_ meta write
- ImportJob.php:478 items() json_decodes the whole file each step
- ImportJob.php:491 new Importer per step, so guid_map() selects all GUIDs each step

Plugin screens: ImportJob.php:658-666 client_state() calls get_edit_post_link per log entry (up to 50). AdminPages script_data passes it on every plugin screen (AdminPages.php:217).
reproduction:
SAVEQUERIES breakdown of a 10-new-episode step at 5000 (summary-5000.txt): 825 queries / 282.9 ms total:
- Importer->write 230
- Importer->create 172
- Feed::flush_cache 160
- Importer->current 80
- sync_duration_seconds 50

Step cost grows with N:
- create steps: median 294/299/349 ms, peak 6.1/9.1/26.2 MB at 100/1000/5000
- unchanged re-import steps: 63/75/128 ms

Job file: 1.1 MB at 1000 and 5.7 MB at 5000; json_decode per step 4.8 ms/+4.3 MB and 25.6 ms/+21.4 MB (perf/jobfile-cost.txt).

Import wall time over AJAX: 4.0 s (10 steps), 36.4 s (100 steps), 206.2 s (500 steps); re-import 1.5/14.0/98.1 s.

Distribution screen: 50 queries in ImportJob::client_state.
user_impact: About 19% of import queries are wasted on cache flushes. Per-step memory and time grow with catalog size; at 5000 items each step re-reads 5.7 MB. These are minor today but compound with IMP-04/IMP-N1 limits.
proposed_fix: Suspend feed-cache flushing during an import step and flush once per step. Keep the item array on a stable offset (for example JSONL with byte offsets, or chunked files). Cache the GUID map in the job or query only the batch's GUIDs. Prime post caches for the log IDs in client_state().
test_plan: Integration test counting queries per 10-item step (no Feed::flush_cache per meta). Benchmark step time at 1000 and 5000 items stays flat.
notes: tests/integration/import-overhead.php: original 1.3.0 makes 140 invalidations and 50 cold-log post reads; current code makes one of each. tests/integration/import.php verifies bounded GUID lookups; tests/perf/run.sh passes the 1000/4000-item step-memory comparison and multi-request preview budget.

title: Switching to 'Another podcast host' saves and activates the permanent 301 without fetching the address; readiness then shows a green 'In sync'
evidence: includes/Hosting.php:184-233 sanitize() only shape-checks: `$out['feed_url'] = self::sanitize_feed_url(...)` (no fetch); includes/Hosting.php:333-346 feed_redirect_target(): `if ( ! self::is_external() || ! self::get( 'redirect' ) ) return ''; ... return $target;` (redirect live as soon as the option is saved); admin/views/hosting.php:55-56 form posts straight to options.php; admin/js/epm-hosting.js:92-107 only toggles fields (no check before submit); includes/Readiness.php:341 `$add( 'ok', __( 'Host feed' ...), $feed );`, :367 `$add( 'ok', __( 'Site feed' ...), __( 'Redirects permanently to your host’s feed.' ...) )`, :419 `'ready' => 0 === $errors`, :451 badge `Hosting::is_external() ? __( 'In sync' ...)`. docs/HOSTING.md:178-185 says the field 'also accepts an Apple Podcasts show link / web page'; only the import card's locate() resolves those.
reproduction:
scratch/audit/feed/hosting-switch.sh [URL]. It logs in as admin, takes the epm_hosting_group nonce from admin.php?page=epm-hosting and POSTs to wp-admin/options.php with mode=external, redirect=1. Afterwards it restores the hosting and sync-state options.

(a) URL = https://feeds.example.test/typo-does-not-exist.xml. Hosting::fetch() of it returns 'HTTP status 404'. Observed:
- options.php -> /wp-admin/admin.php?page=epm-hosting&settings-updated=true
- no notice of any kind on the page
- GET /podcast/feed/ -> '301 -> https://feeds.example.test/typo-does-not-exist.xml'
- dashboard badges 'Configured' and 'In sync' (epm-badge--ok)
- Readiness::report(): ready=true errors=0 warnings=1, [ok] Host feed: https://feeds.example.test/typo-does-not-exist.xml, [ok] Site feed: Redirects permanently to your host’s feed.

(b) URL = https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/synthetic-show/id1000000001 (an Apple show link, which docs/HOSTING.md section 3 says the field accepts). Observed: GET /podcast/feed/ -> '301 -> https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/synthetic-show/id1000000001', badge 'In sync', ready=true.
user_impact: This is the 'move away' journey, docs/HOSTING.md section 7 step 4 ('Switch to Another podcast host … keep the redirect on'). A typo, a dashboard URL or an Apple/Spotify page link immediately sends every app and directory a permanent 301 to something that is not a feed. Apps that follow a 301 rewrite their stored subscription, so listeners can be lost permanently. Nothing on screen says the address was never read: the readiness report and badge say everything is fine until the first scheduled sync (at least 1 minute later, and only if WP-Cron runs) records an error.
proposed_fix:
Validate before switching:
- In Hosting::sanitize() (or a pre_update_option_epm_hosting filter), when mode becomes external or feed_url changes, run Hosting::locate() and FeedParser::parse().
- Store the resolved feed address (Apple link or web page → real feed).
- On failure keep the previous mode/address and add a settings error with the fetch message.
- Track validated_feed_url + validated_at in epm_sync_state. feed_redirect_target() returns '' unless feed_url equals the validated address.
- Readiness: 'Host feed' is ok only when the last successful fetch matches the stored URL. 'Not synced yet' blocks the 'In sync' badge (pending state, not ok).
- Show an explicit success or error notice after saving.
test_plan:
- Integration (hosting.php): EPM_Test_HTTP route answering 404 → update_option through Hosting::sanitize with mode=external. Assert the mode stays 'self' (or the previous URL is kept), feed_redirect_target() === '', and a settings error was added.
- Integration: Apple link → stored feed_url is the lookup result.
- Integration: Readiness::report()['ready'] === false before the first successful sync.
- HTTP suite: after an invalid save, /podcast/feed/ still answers 200.
- e2e setup.mjs: the Hosting form shows an inline error for a 404 address.
notes: tests/integration/audit-sync.php (actual settings save rejects 404 and web pages before enabling a 301; accepts a verified feed; original settings handler fails)

title: Old host 301 → this site while in external mode: infinite redirect loop for apps; the sync never detects the move ('Too many redirects')
evidence: includes/Hosting.php:558-567 fetch() follows redirects inside Requests: `wp_safe_remote_get( $url, [ ... 'redirection' => 5, ... ] )`. It reaches this site's own feed, which in external mode 301s back (includes/Feed.php:591-595 `wp_redirect( $redirect, 301 ...)`), so the moved-here check at includes/Hosting.php:937-949 (`$own_feed = ... self::is_own_feed( $next_url ); $moved_here = $own_feed && 'external' === $settings['mode'];`) is never reached. The docs promise otherwise: docs/HOSTING.md:258-261 ('the next sync switches the site to This website') and :530-533 ('If it happens anyway, the next sync notices the redirect to this site's feed and switches back'); docs/VERIFICATION-1.3.0.md:86 lists 'a redirect to this site switching to This website' as verified. tests/integration/hosting.php:1857-1902 covers only the <itunes:new-feed-url> form and an emulated 301 to another fixture URL; a real request never goes to this site.
reproduction:
Fake old host: scratch/audit/feed/hostsrv/router.php on php -S localhost:8969 (start-fake-host.sh). Mode file 'feed' serves paged-2.xml; mode '301' answers /host.xml with 'Location: http://localhost:8927/podcast/feed/'.

Script: /tmp/epm-a-feed/wp eval-file scratch/audit/feed/moved-by-301.php. It sets external mode with feed_url=http://localhost:8969/host.xml and redirect on, then runs Hosting::sync(true) twice. Test-harness only: reject_unsafe_urls=false for the two local ports, because wp_safe_remote_get refuses other local ports.

Baseline (mode feed): 'sync #1: ok / 2 new episodes.', mode stays external.

Mode 301:
- own feed answers '301 -> http://localhost:8969/host.xml'
- 'sync #1: error / The feed could not be loaded: Too many redirects'
- 'sync #2: error / The feed could not be loaded: Too many redirects'
- 'mode after sync: external / redirect target: http://localhost:8969/host.xml'
- state status=error failures=2
- the host access log shows 6 GETs of /host.xml per sync

An app following redirects: curl -sL --max-redirs 10 http://localhost:8969/host.xml → '301 after 10 redirects'.
user_impact: Journey 'move an existing podcast here'. A show that was mirrored and then redirected at the old host is unreachable in every podcast app (endless 301 loop) until the admin finds the problem and switches the mode by hand. This happens when the user sets the host's 301 before the plugin's move import has switched the site, or after a cancelled or partial move. The sync backs off (1–24 h) and the notice only says 'Too many redirects'. The documented safety net does not exist.
proposed_fix:
Follow redirects manually in Hosting::fetch():
- Use redirection 0 and a loop of up to 5 hops, using the same safe-URL validation per hop.
- Before requesting each Location, check is_own_feed(Location). If it matches, stop and return ['moved_here' => true] without requesting it, so sync() switches to self (and says so).
- Keep the https→http and permanent-only rules per hop.
- Make is_own_feed() also match www/non-www and siteurl/home variants.
- Docs: tell users to switch to 'This website' (or finish the move import) before setting the host's 301.
test_plan:
- Real-socket integration test, not pre_http_request emulation: start a php -S fake host from the test (as in hostsrv/router.php) that 301s to the site's own feed URL. Run Hosting::sync(). Expect mode 'self', feed_redirect_target() '' and a message naming the move. Then curl -L of the host URL ends at 200 on the site's feed.
- Keep the existing new-feed-url test.
notes: tests/media/downloads.php feed-loop (real host-to-site 301 loop fails before the guard, passes with one host request on WordPress 6.2 and 7.1.2); tests/integration/hosting.php

title: Archive feed variants are answered by WordPress core's own conditional-GET (304) before the plugin runs: stale feed and a 304 instead of the hosting 301
evidence: includes/Feed.php:84 `add_action( 'template_redirect', [ $this, 'maybe_render' ], 1 );` and :147-153 `return is_feed() && is_post_type_archive( EpisodePostType::CPT );`. These run after WP::send_headers(). wp-includes/class-wp.php:467-538 (WP 7.1.2): for any request with query_vars['feed'] it computes `$wp_last_modified = ... get_lastpostmodified( 'GMT' )` and `if ( ( $client_last_modified && $client_etag ) ? (...) : ( ( $client_modified_timestamp >= $wp_modified_timestamp ) || ( $client_etag === $wp_etag ) ) ) { $status = 304; $exit_required = true; }`, then exits. Under plain permalinks the episode archive's core discovery link is exactly such a URL: `<link rel="alternate" ... title="EPM Test » Episodes Feed" href="http://localhost:8927/?post_type=podcast_episode&feed=rss2" />`.
reproduction:
Script: scratch/audit/feed/archive-304.sh, pretty permalinks. For /podcast/rss2/:
- plugin LM=Thu, 01 Oct 2026 05:54:18 GMT
- rename the channel via update_option(epm_podcast_settings)
- an If-Modified-Since-only request answers '304' with WordPress's own 'Last-Modified: Thu, 01 Oct 2026 05:54:10 GMT ETag: "53b13800..."', although an unconditional GET shows the new title 'Renamed show 1790834144'
- with hosting switched to external + redirect: IMS request answers '304', unconditional request '301 https://feeds.example.test/synthetic/locked-show.xml'

Same steps on /podcast/feed/: 200 with a new Last-Modified, and 301 in external mode (correct).

Plain permalinks, ?post_type=podcast_episode&feed=rss2 after a channel change with an IMS-only request: 304.
user_impact: Apps or crawlers that subscribed through an archive variant and send only If-Modified-Since never see channel changes (artwork, title, new-feed-url, lock). After a hosting switch they get 304 instead of the 301, so they never move to the host's feed. Under plain permalinks this is the URL WordPress itself advertises on the episode archive. Clients that send both validators are not affected (WordPress requires both to match).
proposed_fix: Take archive-feed requests for the episode post type away from core before send_headers. On the 'request' filter (or at the end of 'parse_request'), when query_vars['post_type'] === CPT and query_vars['feed'] is set and no other archive filters are set, unset 'feed' and set epm_podcast_feed=1, so WP::send_headers treats the request as a non-feed. maybe_render() then serves or redirects with the plugin's own validators. Alternatively, filter post_type_archive_feed_link so it always points at Feed::url().
test_plan:
HTTP suite, for /podcast/rss2/, /podcast/feed/atom/ and ?post_type=podcast_episode&feed=rss2 under both permalink modes:
- channel change + If-Modified-Since only → 200 with the new Last-Modified
- external mode + If-Modified-Since → 301 to the host feed
- the response ETag equals the /podcast/feed/ ETag

reproduction:
/tmp/epm-a-feed/wp eval-file scratch/audit/feed/server-check.php [prefix]

Site 1 (seeded; the newest published episode is 'WAV only', which is not in the feed): feed enclosure http://localhost:8927/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/epm-episode-3.mp3, but the check reports '[ok] Audio (HEAD): 47 KB, audio/wav.'

Run HEAD (following redirects) and a byte-range GET on that exact URL. Validate the Content-Range (start, end and total) and the Content-Length against <enclosure length>. Print the episode title and the URL tested. Optionally test the artwork URL with HEAD as well (Apple requires it).

title: Sync adopts the host's <itunes:new-feed-url> (or a 301 final URL) as the new feed address and 301 target without fetching it; reports 'ok'
evidence: includes/Hosting.php:937-954: `if ( '' !== (string) $parsed['channel']['new_feed_url'] ) { $next_url = self::sanitize_feed_url( ... ); } ... } elseif ( ! $own_feed && '' !== $next_url && $next_url !== $url && ... ) { $settings['feed_url'] = $next_url; update_option( self::OPTION, $settings ); }`. No request is made to $next_url. The message is only the summary (:957 `self::summary( $result )`).
reproduction:
/tmp/epm-a-feed/wp eval-file scratch/audit/feed/sync-new-feed-url.php. The host route serves paged-2.xml with <itunes:new-feed-url>https://feeds.example.test/audit/typo-new-address.xml</itunes:new-feed-url>. Output:
- 'sync status: ok / 2 new episodes.'
- 'stored feed_url now: https://feeds.example.test/audit/typo-new-address.xml'
- 'redirect target now: https://feeds.example.test/audit/typo-new-address.xml'
- 'requests made: GET https://feeds.example.test/audit/host.xml' (the new address was never requested)
- 'what the adopted address answers: …HTTP status 404'

Apps are sent to a dead address. The admin is told 'ok' and only sees errors after the next run. There is no record of the previous address to go back to.

test_plan:
Integration (hosting.php):
- new-feed-url route 404 → feed_url unchanged, status 'warning' with message
- new-feed-url route serving a valid feed → adopted, message names the new address
- a 301 hop to an unparseable page → not adopted
notes: tests/integration/audit-sync.php (same candidate verification as SYNC-N3; original sync fails)

reproduction:
Script: scratch/audit/feed/future-lastmod.sh (re-seeds and deletes epm_feed_build first). Output:
1. 'seeded, Last-Modified: Thu, 01 Oct 2026 06:14:16 GMT'

3. episode set back to future: 'Last-Modified: Fri, 01 Oct 2027 06:14:14 GMT; lastBuildDate: Fri, 01 Oct 2027 06:14:14 +0000'

title: If-None-Match parsing: '*' not honored, and any tag merely containing the hash matches
evidence: includes/Feed.php:612-614 `if ( '' !== $if_none_match ) { $not_modified = false !== strpos( $if_none_match, trim( $etag, '"' ) ); }`
reproduction:
curl http://localhost:8927/podcast/feed/ with ETag "2e495b06c576d960e56af04a55e1194b":
- 'If-None-Match: *' → 'HTTP/1.1 200 OK'. RFC 9110 §13.1.2: for GET/HEAD the condition is false when a representation exists, so the answer should be 304.
- 'If-None-Match: "xx2e495b06c576d960e56af04a55e1194byy"' → 'HTTP/1.1 304 Not Modified'
- Correct: exact, list ('"abc", <etag>') and weak ('W/<etag>') → 304; stale → 200; INM takes precedence over IMS → 200.
user_impact: Small: standards deviations with no known podcast client affected.
proposed_fix: Split the header on commas, trim, strip the W/ prefix and compare whole entity-tags. Treat '*' as a match.
test_plan: HTTP suite: '*' → 304, a tag that only contains the hash → 200, list and weak forms → 304.

title: Episode embed never shows on another WordPress site: the bridge reads the first #?secret= instead of the last, and the title link is swallowed
evidence: assets/js/epm-embed.js:26 `var match = /secret=([\w]{10})/.exec(window.location.hash || '');` takes the FIRST secret. When another WordPress site embeds the URL, the iframe src carries two secrets, e.g. `.../embed/#?secret=9hlhgJwlo8#?secret=yCj6IhZQgP` with `data-secret="yCj6IhZQgP"`: the provider's from the oEmbed response, then the one the consumer's wp_filter_oembed_result appends. Core's wp-includes/js/wp-embed-template.js:232 uses the greedy `window.location.hash.replace( /.*secret=([\d\w]{10}).*/, '$1' )`, so it takes the last one. Because of the wrong secret, the host's wp-embed.js (`iframe[data-secret="…"]` lookup) never removes `position:absolute; visibility:hidden`. In addition, epm-embed.js:51-63 onClick calls `send('link', href); e.preventDefault();` with the same wrong secret, so the title link inside the card is dead.
reproduction:
1. Second site: `WP_DIR=/tmp/epm-a-ux-2 WP_PORT=8968 tests/bin/setup-wp.sh`, then `/tmp/epm-a-ux-2/wp plugin deactivate elementor-podcast-manager`. The mu-plugin `scratch/mu/epm-ux-site2.php` allows port 8928 for the oEmbed fetch.
2. Posts on site 2 created with `wp post create` containing the episode URL http://localhost:8928/podcast/folge-1-erste-schritte/ on its own line (classic) and as a wp:embed block; a control post embeds http://localhost:8928/hello-world/.
3. `node dbg-site2.mjs` output:
   - control core post: `{"style":null,"visible":"visible","bqDisplay":"none"}`
   - episode (classic): `{"style":"position: absolute; visibility: hidden;","visible":"hidden","bqDisplay":"block","msgs":["{\"message\":\"height\",\"value\":200,\"secret\":\"9hlhgJwlo8\"}"...]}` while the iframe's data-secret is yCj6IhZQgP. The block embed behaves the same.
4. `node embed-site2-fixcheck.mjs` serves epm-embed.js with the greedy regex in flight:
   - as shipped: `{"iframeStyle":"position: absolute; visibility: hidden;","blockquote":"block"} title link -> null`
   - patched: `{"iframeStyle":null,"height":"200","blockquote":"none"} title link -> http://localhost:8928/podcast/folge-1-erste-schritte/`
Screenshot: screens/embed-site2-unpatched-top.png (only the fallback link 'Folge 1: Erste Schritte' is visible).
user_impact: "Pasted into another WordPress site, an episode URL becomes a playable card" (README) fails on every WordPress-to-WordPress embed: visitors see a plain link instead of the player. If the card is made visible some other way, its title link does nothing. VERIFICATION-1.3.0 notes that the handshake was only simulated with a single secret.
proposed_fix: Parse the last secret as core does: `/.*secret=([\w]{10})/` (or `hash.replace(/.*secret=([\d\w]{10}).*/, '$1')`), and re-read it on hashchange. Only call preventDefault() in onClick after a successful handshake, i.e. once a 'ready' message with the matching secret has been received; otherwise let the link use target=_top or _blank.
test_plan: An e2e test with a real second WordPress site (or a host page that uses core's wp-embed.js and an iframe src with two #?secret= parts): the iframe loses its hidden style, its height follows the card, the blockquote hides, and clicking the title navigates the top window. Unit-level: the parser returns the last secret for '#?secret=AAAAAAAAAA#?secret=BBBBBBBBBB'. Keep the single-secret case.
notes: Root cause shown by an in-flight patch, not by a repo change. The embed works on plain HTML pages without a secret (see UX-N13).
validation: tests/e2e/frontend.mjs (two secrets, matching parent handshake, hash changes)

- admin/js/epm-hosting.js:484-498

Check the execCommand return value. The three screens could enqueue the shared admin copy helper instead of three copies.

title: Design screen has duplicate IDs (_wpnonce, submit)
evidence: admin/views/design.php:189, 446, 452 `wp_nonce_field(...)` (each prints id="_wpnonce"); 377, 447, 456 `submit_button( …, 'submit', false )` (each prints id="submit").
